messages.text: hi,  i just got my bs4.  It looks great.  It is currently up and running.  the dashboard on the web as well as the led on the miner say its running at 19TH.  However it is on stock settings and only running 250w 650 frequency and 1150 voltage.  while the miner says its running 19th my mining pool and my hashwatcher both say its only running at 9.7 TH  i haven't swapped the OS out to harlo yet because my mining tools like the standard os and i wanted to make sure it worked before changing the OS
Hi, I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. One moment while I check the BS-4's listed specs.
Read the bitfortun bs4 page
Searched the web · BitFortun BS-4 hashrate pool reported half

Hi, I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Glad the BS-4 arrived and is running.

The pool's number is the one to trust. Your miner works out its 19 TH/s itself, usually from clock speed times chip count, so it shows what the chips *should* do. The pool counts the shares it actually receives, so 9.7 TH/s is what is really reaching it. Your BS-4 is rated at 
18 TH/s
 from 
four BM1373 chips, 4.5 TH out of each one
.

9.7 is almost exactly half of 19. That can mean two of the four chips aren't producing accepted work. It can also just be a reporting issue: BitFortun already had a problem on the BS-1 and BS-2 where the screen showed more hashrate than the units really did.

Before we read too much into it, it helps to rule out the simple causes. Can you tell me:

1. **How long has it been running on the pool?** Pool averages are noisy for the first hour or so. Is the pool's 9.7 a 10-minute, 1-hour or 24-hour average?
2. **What does the miner's web UI show for chips?** Does it detect all 4 ASICs? If it shows per-chip hashrate or error rate, are any chips at zero or much lower than the rest?
3. **Rejected shares and firmware:** what share count and reject percentage does the dashboard show, and which firmware version is it running?

A screenshot of the dashboard would cover most of this. Please leave the stock settings alone for now so we're testing a known baseline.

On your plan to switch to Harlo OS: waiting is fine. Harlo OS works out 
hash from the shares your pool accepts
, so it would show you the real number either way.

I searched for that exact log line in BitFortun's material and in the open-source ESP-Miner code that this kind of firmware is usually built on. Nothing I found documents "respnse for invalid asic", so I can't tell you for certain what it means and I won't guess.

Here is what the sources do show. On this firmware family, the hashrate monitor 
reads the per-chip nonce/hash counter (0x90) to derive per-chip hashrate
. So these errors come from the part of the firmware that measures each chip's real output. Your BS-4 has four chips, and the log names "asic 4" and "asic 6". That's worth chasing, because it could link to the 19 vs 9.7 gap. I can't confirm that link until I see a bit more.

30 minutes is also early to judge. Let it keep running on stock settings. Meanwhile, two things:

1. **Firmware version:** what does the System or Settings page in the web UI show? Copy it exactly, including any build date.
2. **The startup lines in the log:** restart the miner and copy the first lines that mention ASICs or chips. Look for something like a chip count or "detected" line. Those show how many chips the firmware actually finds on the board.

After that, once it has run for a full hour, tell me the pool's 1-hour average. A screenshot of the log works fine if that's easier than copying it.

Searched the web · NerdQAxePlus "nonce distribution" history log per asic

Thanks, that log helps a lot. Look at this line, which repeats all the way through:

`history: nonce distribution: 22/14/0/0`

There are four numbers, one for each of your four chips. In this firmware family that line counts the nonces each chip has returned. A healthy multi-chip board shows them spread evenly. For example, a report on another ESP-Miner-based 9-chip board lists its nonce distribution as even across all 9 chips.

On yours, the first two chips are finding work (22 and 14 nonces) and the last two show 0. That matches your numbers: two of four chips working gives about half of 19 TH/s, which is your pool's 9.7. It also fits the earlier "invalid asic" errors. The miner's 19 TH/s is a calculated figure, so it doesn't notice two chips sitting idle.

What the log can't tell us yet is the cause: firmware or board. These are the safe checks you can do:

1. **Full power cycle:** turn the PSU off at the wall, wait 30 seconds, power back on. Watch the "nonce distribution" line for 5 to 10 minutes. Does it stay at x/x/0/0?
2. **The boot lines:** from the very top of the log after that restart, copy the lines about chip detection or chip count. Those show whether the firmware finds all 4 chips at startup.
3. **Stay on stock:** keep the stock settings and firmware for now, and don't change frequency or voltage to try to wake the chips.

Your temperatures look healthy at about 40.6 C. One thing to mention to JD: both fans are set to 100%, but fan 0 reads 2495 RPM and fan 1 reads 1215 RPM.

JD already has your case. Please add this "0/0" log to the Discord thread at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf with @nullhashrate. That's the quickest way to get his eyes on it, and the team's answer will still come to your email.

**How to post it on Discord, step by step:**

1. Open this link on your phone or computer: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf
2. If you don't have a Discord account, it will ask you to make a free one (email, username, password). If you do, just log in.
3. Click **Accept Invite** to join our server.
4. On the left is a list of channels (names starting with #). Pick the one for support or help. If you can't tell which one, use the Harlo OS channel. JD reads it too.
5. Click the message box at the bottom, type **@nullhashrate** and click his name when it pops up.
6. Paste the message below after his name and press Enter.

**Ready-to-paste message:**

> New Bitfortun BS-4, stock firmware v1.3, stock settings (650 MHz / 1150 mV, ~250 W). Screen says 19 TH/s, pool and HashWatcher say 9.7 TH/s. No problem. You don't need to copy anything. Here are two easier ways:

**Option 1: type a short message.** In the Discord support channel, type this yourself:

> @nullhashrate New BS-4, stock firmware 1.3. Pool shows 9.7 TH, screen shows 19 TH. Log says nonce distribution x/x/0/0, chips 3 and 4 dead. Same after several restarts. HeliumDeploy has the details.

**Option 2: post a screenshot.** Take a photo or screenshot of the miner's log page where the "nonce distribution ... /0/0" line shows. In Discord, click the **+** next to the message box and choose the image. Then type **@nullhashrate BS-4, chips 3 and 4 at 0** and press Enter.

You also don't have to post on Discord at all. JD already has your full case from me, including the logs and your restarts. Discord just tends to get you an answer faster.
